recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No additional core source change is recommended for FHIR-51608 unless FHIR-I later decides to further constrain optional server-specific behavior for compartment-qualified operation URLs.
issue_request: FHIR-51608 was Applied as Persuasive with Modification for R6. It asked the HTTP, Search, and CompartmentDefinition guidance to clarify that compartment-qualified URLs are a search view rather than an alternate resource identity: search bundles should use native, non-compartment-specific full URLs, references in returned resources should not be rewritten into compartment paths, and only search is defined as a compartment interaction while operations through compartment-qualified links are not defined.
initial_application: The source was already changed by 7737bfeea16cc151563f253dfa404f58eacc9a5f and merged through PR #3967 by 2ec3e732369b18cd589904205b73b4237f850e82. That application updated source/compartmentdefinition/compartmentdefinition-notes.xml, source/http.html, and source/search.html, but did not include a parseable Issue-Reconcile-Key trailer.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2025-08-18 record the work group continuing FHIR-51608 from the prior week, adding search-page guidance, HTTP examples and links, a Compartment Interactions row in the HTTP introduction, and a note that operations via a compartment are not defined; the motion passed Persuasive with Modification 13-0-0. The edited files are in current build scope: source/fhir.ini has active CompartmentDefinition entries, and http.html and search.html are the core REST and Search pages referenced by the issue.
reconciliation: No source edits were made in this reconciliation. The current combined branch already says compartment search outcomes match equivalent system/type searches with non-compartment-specific full URLs, returned references are not rewritten into compartment paths, HTTP lists compartment search as the compartment interaction, and CompartmentDefinition says reads, writes, history, operations, and batch/transaction POSTs are not defined through compartment-qualified URLs.
